top.line: Ten agents in sequence on schedules: brittle without session continuity, records and visibility; next, a dedicated account.
top.para: The PHP story runs a pipeline of about ten scheduled agents, 11 schedules and 53 wakes a day. Each needs its own readable session holding state, keys and vaults. Scheduling into a chosen session made it possible, but it remains brittle. I go slowly, lean on the platform, invest in visibility, and plan a dedicated account.

in-short.line: Eight lines: the pipeline, sessions, the old scheduling, the new, brittleness, pace, visibility, a dedicated account.
in-short.para: Ten agents run in sequence unattended. Each needs its own session I can open. Scheduling once opened a new session per run, which did not scale. Scheduling into a chosen session made it work. This morning 5 wakes met and 11 missed. I go slowly, use the platform, spend as much on visibility, and plan a dedicated account.

what-we-run.line: Researcher, curator, journalist and correspondent run in sequence, then the Sherpa, desk, librarian and ontologist.
what-we-run.para: Each stage reads only the previous one's vault or output. Some agents wake three or four times a day, others once; the schedule page shows 11 active schedules and 53 wakes a day. The aim is not maximum frequency but reliable runs that happen when nobody is watching, removing me from the loop.

needs.line: Each wake should land in the same session, keeping secrets, state and gigabytes of vault data, and stay readable.
needs.para: Running every wake in one session per agent keeps its keys, its state and its data in place, avoiding repeated clones of gigabytes. Each stage writes to its own vault; the researcher's reached 63,662 objects and broke sgit until pack mode fixed it. Continuing the same session also keeps the agent's history readable.

history.line: Tools in the loop, then scheduled runs opening new sessions, then scheduling into a chosen, briefed session.
history.para: The tool loop made an agent a session. Scheduling followed, but each cloud run opened a new session, so secrets and state restarted and sessions piled up. Recently I found I could schedule into a specific session: briefed, given its key by QR handshake, with repositories and vaults already cloned, every wake arrives ready.

brittle.line: A schedule once fired in the wrong environment; this morning 11 of 16 wakes left no run record.
brittle.para: An agent trying to set its own schedule fired it in the wrong place. The control room showed 5 wakes met and 11 missed, but the researcher and curator had worked, promoting 18 sources, without leaving records. The fix was small wake prompts, a shared wake procedure ending in a run record, and publishing records without a release.

platform.line: Platform-provided features beat home-made wiring because the platform maintains them; I code only the gaps.
platform.para: I have wired such systems myself before, but it works better when the platform provides the service and maintains it. So I live with platform limits, code only what is missing on top, and aim to delete that code later because every line is something I must maintain.

slowly.line: Going slowly buys understanding, confidence and infrastructure, the explorer-to-villager path.
slowly.para: Pace is chosen, not forced: it builds the control and visibility that let agents take more agency and more loops run. This explorer workflow will become product and code over time, but only by running it, experimenting and mapping it until it earns the confidence of products and commodities.

visibility.line: Visualisation and checks are half the work: the schedule, the control room and the desk show the system.
visibility.para: The PHP agents built a schedule page with cards, wakes and runs, a control room with the pipeline, timeline and pending decisions, and a desk showing the pipeline and the correspondent's catches. I spend as much time making the environment visible and controlled as building it.

dedicated.line: Move the team to a dedicated account for isolation, cost control, usage and model visibility.
dedicated.para: Running everything in my main account clutters my sessions and lacks isolation. A dedicated account, perhaps a Team seat, would contain the flows and make costs, usage and models clear. Most work is done; what remains is tightening, deleting what is unneeded, and earning resilience by running continuously.

unit.line: Platform builders should let users create complete separate instances, because the unit of work is the platform.
unit.para: Customers need parts of everything a platform does, so the unit is not an arbitrary user session but the whole platform. Like a new Claude session or an AWS account, users need full, separate instances that run wherever they are needed. I am about to use that pattern for the PHP team.

limits.line: Timings are this pipeline's; scheduling history is my experience; the misfire is unrecorded; the account is planned.
limits.para: A day and a half to reliability measures this pipeline, not the platform. The documentation still describes a new session per cloud run, and I do not know when targeted scheduling arrived. The misfire comes from my session. The dedicated account is a plan. 'Missed' means no run record within 45 minutes.

sources.line: My memos; the PHP site's schedule, control room and desk at v0.19.1; Claude Code's scheduling docs.
sources.para: My two voice memos of 25 October 2026; the PHP story site's schedule, control room and journalist's desk at release v0.19.1, with screenshots under Apache-2.0; Claude Code's documentation on cloud and session-scoped scheduled tasks; and related articles on the QR handshake, pack mode, frozen teams and explorer coding.
